plants.name: Ashwagandha
plants.detailedPreparation: For decoction: Boil 1 teaspoon of dried ashwagandha root in 2 cups of water for 10-15 minutes. Strain and drink warm. For powder: Mix 1/2 to 1 teaspoon with warm milk or water. Best taken in the evening.
plants.dosage: Powder 3–6 g/day; Standardized extract per label
plants.detailedDosage: General health: 300-500mg twice daily. For stress and anxiety: 600mg daily. For sleep: Take 300-500mg 30 minutes before bedtime. Always start with lower dose and gradually increase.
plants.safety: May potentiate sedatives and thyroid meds; avoid in pregnancy unless supervised
plants.contraindications: Not recommended during pregnancy. Use with caution if taking sedatives, thyroid medication, or immunosuppressants. May lower blood sugar - monitor if diabetic.

plants.name: Tulsi
plants.detailedPreparation: For tea: Steep 5-10 fresh leaves or 1 tsp dried leaves in hot water for 5-10 minutes. Add honey if desired. For juice: Crush fresh leaves and extract juice. Mix with honey or water.
plants.detailedDosage: Tea: 2-3 cups daily. Juice: 5-10ml twice daily. Powder: 1-3g daily with water or honey. For diabetes: Take before meals.
plants.safety: May lower blood sugar; caution with anticoagulants
plants.contraindications: May interact with blood-thinning medications. Not recommended for people with bleeding disorders. May lower blood sugar levels significantly.

plants.name: Turmeric
plants.detailedPreparation: Golden milk: Mix 1 tsp turmeric powder with 1/4 tsp black pepper in 1 cup milk. Heat gently. For paste: Mix with water or oil. For wounds: Apply paste directly.
plants.dosage: Powder: 1–3 g/day; With black pepper for absorption
plants.detailedDosage: General use: 500mg-1g, 2-3 times daily. With black pepper (piperine) for enhanced absorption. For arthritis: 500mg capsules 3 times daily.
plants.safety: High doses may cause gastric upset
plants.contraindications: May cause gallbladder contractions. Avoid if you have gallstones or bile duct obstruction. High doses may interact with blood thinners.

plants.name: Brahmi
plants.detailedPreparation: Juice: Extract from fresh leaves, mix with water. Powder: Can be taken with ghee, honey or water. Best taken after meals.
plants.detailedDosage: Standardized extract (20% bacosides): 300-450mg daily. Powder: 1-2g twice daily with warm milk. For children: Half the adult dose.
plants.safety: May cause nausea in empty stomach
plants.contraindications: May interact with thyroid medications. Not recommended for people with digestive issues or ulcers. May slow heart rate - use caution with heart conditions.

plants.name: Guduchi
plants.detailedPreparation: Decoction: Boil 1 tsp dried stem in 2 cups water until reduced to half. Strain and drink. Powder: Can be taken with honey or water.
plants.detailedDosage: Powder: 1-2g, 2-3 times daily. Tablet: 1-2 tablets (500mg each) twice daily. For diabetes: Take before meals.
plants.contraindications: Generally safe. Rare cases of allergic reactions reported. May lower blood sugar levels - monitor if diabetic.

plants.name: Shatavari
plants.detailedPreparation: Milk decoction: Boil 1 tsp powder in milk. Strain and drink. With ghee: Mix with equal part ghee. Can be taken with honey or water.
plants.detailedDosage: General use: 1-2g, 2-3 times daily. For lactation: 3g twice daily with milk. For hormonal balance: 500mg-1g twice daily.
plants.contraindications: Not recommended for estrogen-sensitive conditions. Use with caution if you have kidney issues. May cause allergic reactions in some individuals.

plants.name: Neem
plants.detailedPreparation: Juice: Crush fresh leaves and extract juice. Mix with water. For skin: Apply oil directly or mix with coconut oil. Powder: Can be taken with water.
plants.detailedDosage: Juice: 2-4ml twice daily. Powder: 500mg-1g twice daily. Oil: For external use only. Capsules: 1-2 capsules (500mg) daily.
plants.contraindications: Not recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding. May lower blood sugar significantly. Long-term internal use may cause liver or kidney damage.

plants.name: Amla
plants.detailedPreparation: Juice: Extract from fresh fruits, mix with water. Powder: Can be taken with water, honey or ghee. Fresh fruit: Can be eaten directly.
plants.detailedDosage: Powder: 1-2g, 2-3 times daily. Juice: 10-20ml daily. Fresh fruit: 1-2 fruits daily. For hair: Apply oil externally.
plants.contraindications: Generally very safe. May cause acidity in some people if taken on empty stomach. No known serious contraindications.

plants.name: Arjuna
plants.detailedPreparation: Decoction: Boil 1 tsp bark powder in 2 cups water until reduced to half. Strain and drink. Powder: Can be taken with warm water or milk.
plants.detailedDosage: Powder: 1-2g, 2-3 times daily. Extract: 500mg twice daily. For heart health: Take consistently for 2-3 months.
plants.contraindications: May interact with blood pressure medications. Not recommended during pregnancy. May cause constipation in some individuals.

plants.name: Guggul
plants.detailedPreparation: Tablets: Take with warm water. Resin: Purified form only. Traditionally taken with triphala or other herbs.
plants.detailedDosage: Standardized extract: 500mg, 2-3 times daily. For cholesterol: Take for 12-24 weeks. For arthritis: Combine with anti-inflammatory herbs.
plants.contraindications: Not recommended during pregnancy. May interact with thyroid medications. Avoid in liver disease or inflammatory bowel conditions.

plants.name: Punarnava
plants.detailedPreparation: Decoction: Boil 1 tsp powder in 2 cups water until reduced to half. Strain and drink. Best taken in morning.
plants.detailedDosage: Powder: 1-2g, 2-3 times daily. Extract: 500mg twice daily. For edema: Take for 2-4 weeks. Increase water intake.
plants.contraindications: Not recommended during pregnancy. May interact with diuretic medications. Use with caution in kidney disease.

plants.name: Shankhpushpi
plants.detailedPreparation: Juice: Extract from fresh plant. Powder: Mix with milk or water. Ghrita: Medicated ghee preparation.
plants.detailedDosage: Powder: 1-2g, 2-3 times daily. Juice: 5-10ml twice daily. For memory: Take consistently for 2-3 months.
plants.contraindications: May enhance effects of sedative medications. Not recommended during pregnancy. Use with caution if driving or operating machinery.

plants.name: Yashtimadhu
plants.detailedPreparation: Decoction: Boil 1 tsp powder in 2 cups water for 10 minutes. Strain and drink. For throat: Gargle with decoction. Chew sticks: Chew slowly.
plants.detailedDosage: Powder: 1-2g, 2-3 times daily. For ulcers: Take between meals. Maximum 4-6 weeks continuous use.
plants.safety: Avoid in hypertension; may cause edema
plants.contraindications: Not recommended for people with high blood pressure, heart conditions, or kidney disease. Avoid during pregnancy. May interact with corticosteroids.

plants.name: Vacha
plants.detailedPreparation: Powder: Only processed form should be used. Mix with honey or ghee. Medicated ghee: Special preparation required.
plants.detailedDosage: Processed powder: 125-250mg, 1-2 times daily. Never exceed 500mg daily. Use only under supervision.
plants.safety: Use processed form only; toxic in high doses
plants.contraindications: Not recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Toxic in high doses. Use only professionally processed forms. Avoid long-term use.

plants.name: Haritaki
plants.detailedPreparation: Powder: Take with warm water or ghee. Decoction: Boil 1 tsp powder in 2 cups water until reduced to half. Strain and drink.
plants.detailedDosage: Powder: 1-2g, 2-3 times daily. For constipation: Take at bedtime. For digestion: Take after meals.
plants.contraindications: Not recommended during pregnancy. May cause dehydration if not taken with sufficient water. Avoid in severe diarrhea or dehydration.

plants.name: Bibhitaki
plants.detailedPreparation: Powder: Take with honey for respiratory issues, with warm water for digestion. Decoction: Boil 1 tsp in 2 cups water.
plants.detailedDosage: Powder: 1-2g, 2 times daily. For respiratory: Mix with honey. For digestion: Take with warm water.
plants.contraindications: Not recommended during pregnancy. May cause excessive dryness. Avoid in already dehydrated conditions.

plants.name: Amalaki
plants.detailedPreparation: Fresh: Eat directly. Powder: Mix with water or honey. Murabba: Ayurvedic preserve, 1-2 pieces daily.
plants.detailedDosage: Powder: 1-2g, 2-3 times daily. Fresh fruit: 1-2 daily. Murabba: 10-20g daily.
plants.safety: Very safe even in high doses
plants.contraindications: Generally very safe. Rare cases of allergic reactions. No known serious contraindications.

plants.name: Gokshura
plants.detailedPreparation: Decoction: Boil 1 tsp powder in 2 cups water until reduced to half. Strain and drink. Powder: Can be taken with milk or water.
plants.detailedDosage: Powder: 1-2g, 2-3 times daily. Extract: 500mg twice daily. For urinary: Increase water intake.
plants.contraindications: Generally safe. May interact with diabetes medications. Use with caution in hormone-sensitive conditions.

plants.name: Manjistha
plants.detailedPreparation: Decoction: Boil 1 tsp powder in 2 cups water for 10 minutes. Strain and drink. For skin: Apply paste externally.
plants.detailedDosage: Powder: 1-2g, 2 times daily. Extract: 500mg twice daily. For skin: Both internal and external use.
plants.contraindications: Not recommended during pregnancy. May interact with blood thinners. Temporary red discoloration of urine is normal.

plants.name: Katuki
plants.detailedPreparation: Powder: Mix with honey to mask bitterness. Decoction: Boil 1/2 tsp in 2 cups water. Very bitter taste.
plants.detailedDosage: Powder: 500mg-1g, 2 times daily. Extract: 250-500mg twice daily. For liver: Take for 4-8 weeks.
plants.contraindications: Not recommended during pregnancy. High doses may cause diarrhea. Use with caution in autoimmune conditions.

plants.name: Pippali
plants.detailedPreparation: Powder: Can be taken with honey. Decoction: Boil 1/2 tsp in 2 cups water. Often combined with other herbs.
plants.detailedDosage: Powder: 500mg-1g, 2 times daily. For respiratory: Mix with honey. For digestion: Take after meals.
plants.safety: Heating effect; balance with cooling foods
plants.contraindications: Not recommended during pregnancy. May increase Pitta. Use with cooling herbs in Pitta constitution.

plants.name: Bala
plants.detailedPreparation: Powder: Can be taken with milk or ghee. Decoction: Boil 1 tsp in 2 cups water. Oil: For external massage.
plants.detailedDosage: Powder: 1-2g, 2-3 times daily. Oil: External use only. For weakness: Long-term use beneficial.
plants.contraindications: Generally safe. No known serious contraindications. Use standard precautions during pregnancy.

plants.name: Daruharidra
plants.detailedPreparation: Eye drops: Professional preparation only. Decoction: Boil 1 tsp in 2 cups water. For skin: Apply paste externally.
plants.detailedDosage: Powder: 500mg-1g, 2 times daily. External use only for eyes. For skin: Apply paste 2-3 times daily.
plants.contraindications: Not recommended during pregnancy. Not for internal use without professional guidance. May cause irritation in sensitive skin.

plants.name: Jatamansi
plants.detailedPreparation: Powder: Can be taken with milk or water. Oil: For external massage, especially head massage.
plants.detailedDosage: Powder: 500mg-1g, 2 times daily. For sleep: Take before bedtime. Oil: External use for massage.
plants.contraindications: May enhance effects of sedative medications. Use with caution if driving or operating machinery. Generally safe.

plants.name: Kutaja
plants.detailedPreparation: Decoction: Boil 1 tsp bark powder in 2 cups water until reduced to half. Strain and drink. Very effective for diarrhea.
plants.detailedDosage: Powder: 1-2g, 2-3 times daily. For acute diarrhea: Every 4-6 hours. Reduce frequency as symptoms improve.
plants.contraindications: Not recommended for long-term use. Use only for acute diarrhea. Discontinue if constipation occurs.

plants.name: Chandana
plants.detailedPreparation: Paste: Mix powder with rose water or milk. Apply externally. Powder: Can be taken with water or milk.
plants.detailedDosage: Powder: 500mg-1g, 2 times daily. External paste: Apply as needed. For Pitta: Best taken in summer.
plants.safety: Very cooling; balance in cold climates
plants.contraindications: Not recommended in Vata disorders or cold climates. May increase coldness. Use with warming herbs in winter.

plants.name: Mustaka
plants.detailedPreparation: Decoction: Boil 1 tsp powder in 2 cups water. Strain and drink. Powder: Can be taken with honey or water.
plants.detailedDosage: Powder: 1-2g, 2-3 times daily. For fever: Take with honey. For diarrhea: Take with buttermilk.
plants.contraindications: May cause excessive dryness. Not recommended in dehydration conditions. Use with hydrating herbs.

plants.name: Sariva
plants.detailedPreparation: Decoction: Boil 1 tsp powder in 2 cups water. Strain and drink. Powder: Can be taken with milk or water.
plants.detailedDosage: Powder: 1-2g, 2-3 times daily. For skin: Both internal and external use. Long-term use beneficial.
plants.contraindications: Generally safe. No known serious contraindications. Use standard precautions during pregnancy.

plants.name: Bhumyamalaki
plants.detailedPreparation: Juice: Extract from fresh plant. Powder: Can be taken with water. Both forms effective for liver disorders.
plants.detailedDosage: Juice: 5-10ml, 2 times daily. Powder: 1-2g, 2 times daily. For liver: Take for 4-8 weeks.
plants.contraindications: Generally safe. May interact with diabetes medications. Monitor blood sugar levels.

plants.name: Danti
plants.detailedPreparation: Only professionally processed form should be used. Never use raw root. Mix with other herbs to reduce potency.
plants.detailedDosage: Processed powder: 125-250mg, once daily. Never exceed 500mg. Use only for short periods.
plants.contraindications: Not recommended during pregnancy. Very strong purgative - use only under professional supervision. May cause dehydration.

plants.name: Eranda
plants.detailedPreparation: Oil: For external massage only. Pills: Professionally prepared. Root: Decoction under guidance.
plants.detailedDosage: Oil: 5-10 drops with warm milk at bedtime. External: Massage affected areas. Root: Only under supervision.
plants.safety: Seeds are toxic; use processed oil only
plants.contraindications: Seeds are highly toxic - never consume raw. Use only professionally processed oil. Not recommended during pregnancy.

plants.name: Gudmar
plants.detailedPreparation: Powder: Can be taken with water. Best taken before meals. Capsules: Standardized extracts available.
plants.detailedDosage: Powder: 1-2g, 2 times daily before meals. Extract: 500mg twice daily. For diabetes: Monitor blood sugar levels.
plants.contraindications: May significantly lower blood sugar. Monitor closely if taking diabetes medications. Not recommended during pregnancy.

plants.name: Kalmegh
plants.detailedPreparation: Juice: Extract from fresh plant. Very bitter. Powder: Can be taken with honey. Capsules available.
plants.detailedDosage: Powder: 500mg-1g, 2-3 times daily. Extract: 300-500mg twice daily. For fever: Take at first signs.
plants.safety: Very bitter; best in capsule form
plants.contraindications: Not recommended during pregnancy. Very bitter - may cause nausea. May interact with blood thinners.

plants.name: Mulethi
plants.detailedPreparation: Decoction: Boil 1 tsp in 2 cups water. Strain and drink. For throat: Gargle with decoction. Chew small pieces.
plants.detailedDosage: Powder: 1-2g, 2-3 times daily. For cough: Mix with honey. Maximum 4-6 weeks continuous use.
plants.contraindications: Not recommended for people with high blood pressure, heart conditions, or kidney disease. Avoid during pregnancy. May interact with corticosteroids.

plants.name: Nagarmotha
plants.detailedPreparation: Decoction: Boil 1 tsp in 2 cups water. Strain and drink. Powder: Can be taken with buttermilk or water.
plants.detailedDosage: Powder: 1-2g, 2-3 times daily. For diarrhea: Take with yogurt or buttermilk.
plants.contraindications: May cause constipation in excess. Not recommended during pregnancy. Use with caution in Vata disorders.

plants.name: Pashanbheda
plants.detailedPreparation: Decoction: Boil 1 tsp in 2 cups water until reduced to half. Strain and drink. Increase water intake.
plants.detailedDosage: Powder: 1-2g, 2-3 times daily. For stones: Take with plenty of water. Use for 4-8 weeks.
plants.contraindications: Not recommended during pregnancy. May interact with diuretic medications. Ensure adequate hydration.

plants.name: Pippalimula
plants.detailedPreparation: Decoction: Boil 1/2 tsp in 2 cups water. Strain and drink. Often combined with honey and ginger.
plants.detailedDosage: Powder: 500mg-1g, 2 times daily. For chronic cough: Take with honey. Long-term use beneficial.
plants.contraindications: Not recommended during pregnancy. May increase Pitta. Use with cooling herbs in Pitta constitution.

plants.name: Rasna
plants.detailedPreparation: Powder: Can be taken with warm water or milk. Oil: For external massage. Often combined with other herbs.
plants.detailedDosage: Powder: 1-2g, 2-3 times daily. Oil: External massage twice daily. For arthritis: Both internal and external use.
plants.contraindications: Generally safe. No known serious contraindications. Use standard precautions during pregnancy.

plants.name: Sarpagandha
plants.detailedPreparation: Only professionally prepared forms should be used. Never self-prescribe. Requires careful dosing.
plants.detailedDosage: Professional preparation only: 125-250mg, 1-2 times daily. Never exceed 500mg. Requires medical supervision.
plants.contraindications: Not for self-medication. Requires professional supervision. Many drug interactions. Not recommended during pregnancy.

plants.name: Shallaki
plants.detailedPreparation: Powder: Can be taken with warm water. Capsules: Standardized extracts available. Often combined with other anti-inflammatories.
plants.detailedDosage: Extract: 300-500mg, 2-3 times daily. Powder: 1-2g, 2-3 times daily. For arthritis: Long-term use beneficial.
plants.contraindications: Generally very safe. Rare cases of stomach discomfort. No known serious contraindications.

plants.name: Tagara
plants.detailedPreparation: Decoction: Boil 1 tsp in 2 cups water. Strain and drink before bedtime. Powder: Can be taken with warm milk.
plants.detailedDosage: Powder: 1-2g at bedtime. Extract: 500mg before sleep. For anxiety: Smaller doses during day.
plants.contraindications: May enhance effects of sedative medications. Not recommended during pregnancy. Use with caution if driving or operating machinery.

plants.name: Talispatra
plants.detailedPreparation: Decoction: Boil 1 tsp in 2 cups water. Strain and drink. Often combined with honey and ginger.
plants.detailedDosage: Powder: 500mg-1g, 2 times daily. For asthma: Take with honey. Long-term use beneficial.
plants.contraindications: Not recommended during pregnancy. May interact with respiratory medications. Use with caution in Pitta conditions.

plants.name: Twak
plants.detailedPreparation: Decoction: Boil 1/2 tsp in 2 cups water. Strain and drink. Powder: Can be added to foods or taken with honey.
plants.detailedDosage: Powder: 500mg-1g, 2 times daily. For digestion: Take after meals. For cold: Add to tea.
plants.contraindications: Not recommended in high Pitta conditions. May interact with blood thinners. Use in moderation.

plants.name: Vamsha
plants.detailedPreparation: Juice: Extract from young shoots. Powder: Can be taken with honey or water. Often combined with other respiratory herbs.
plants.detailedDosage: Juice: 10-20ml, 2 times daily. Powder: 1-2g, 2 times daily. For respiratory: Take with honey.
plants.contraindications: Generally safe. No known serious contraindications. Use standard precautions during pregnancy.

plants.name: Vasa
plants.detailedPreparation: Juice: Extract from fresh leaves. Powder: Can be taken with honey. Decoction: Boil leaves in water.
plants.detailedDosage: Juice: 5-10ml, 2 times daily. Powder: 1-2g, 2 times daily. For asthma: Take with honey.
plants.safety: May cause nausea in high doses
plants.contraindications: Not recommended during pregnancy. May cause nausea in high doses. Use with digestive herbs to reduce side effects.

plants.name: Vidanga
plants.detailedPreparation: Powder: Can be taken with honey or warm water. Pills: Professionally prepared. Often combined with other digestive herbs.
plants.detailedDosage: Powder: 1-2g, 2 times daily. For worms: Take for 3-5 days. Repeat after 2 weeks if needed.
plants.contraindications: Not recommended during pregnancy. For short-term use only. May cause mild digestive discomfort.

plants.name: Yava
plants.detailedPreparation: Water: Soak 1 tbsp seeds in water overnight. Drink water in morning. Porridge: Cook seeds with water or milk.
plants.detailedDosage: Seeds: 50-100g daily as food. Water: 1 glass daily. For diabetes: Replace regular grains with barley.
plants.contraindications: Generally very safe. Rare cases of gluten sensitivity. No known serious contraindications.

plants.name: Haridra
plants.detailedPreparation: Paste: Mix with water or oil. Apply externally. Powder: Can be taken with milk or water. With black pepper for absorption.
plants.detailedDosage: Powder: 1-2g, 2 times daily. With black pepper for enhanced absorption. For wounds: Apply paste directly.
plants.contraindications: May cause gallbladder contractions. Avoid if you have gallstones. High doses may interact with blood thinners.

plants.name: Jambu
plants.detailedPreparation: Seed powder: Dry and powder seeds. Take with water. Fruit: Eat fresh or as juice. Both effective for diabetes.
plants.detailedDosage: Seed powder: 1-2g, 2-3 times daily. Fruit: 50-100g daily. Juice: 50ml twice daily. For diabetes: Take before meals.
plants.contraindications: May significantly lower blood sugar. Monitor closely if taking diabetes medications. Seeds may cause constipation in excess.

plants.name: Kumari
plants.detailedPreparation: Gel: Extract fresh gel from leaves. Apply externally. Juice: Professional preparation only. Latex: Strong purgative - use with caution.
plants.detailedDosage: Juice: 10-20ml daily. Gel: External application as needed. Latex: Only under professional guidance.
plants.safety: Latex is purgative; use gel externally
plants.contraindications: Not recommended during pregnancy. Latex is strong purgative - avoid self-medication. May interact with diabetes medications.
